title: SMTPMonster: a more professional hand
question: Three conventional, polished directions plus the category standard. Pick one or steer again.

options.label: The Transcript
options.thesis: Prove it the way engineers trust: show the SMTP conversation and the exact moment the recipient is rewritten.
options.viewport: Left: headline, one line of copy and the email field. Right: an annotated SMTP session where RCPT TO customer addresses resolve to your inbox, line by line.
options.risk: Familiar to anyone who reads infra docs; the transcript must be the hero, not a decoration.

options.label: The Inbox
options.lineage: Mail client UI: the place the product actually shows up
options.thesis: Your inbox is the UI, so the page shows the inbox: the looped-back message, rendered, with its original recipients on top.
options.viewport: Headline and email field on top; below, a full-width, realistic mail-client pane open on a looped message showing the From/To/CC/BCC block SMTPMonster adds.
options.risk: The most conventional of the three; leans on executing the mail pane with real care.

options.label: The Safety Valve
options.thesis: A calm, serious infrastructure page: one diagram where every outbound path is closed except the one back to you.
options.viewport: Dark navy page; headline and email field above a wide routing diagram: your app on the left, real recipients struck off on the right, a single live path looping back to your inbox.
options.risk: Dark infra pages are common in dev tooling; it earns its place only if the diagram is exact.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: Sits alongside Mailtrap, Postmark and Resend: white page, crisp sans, one brand blue, product screenshot.
canonCard.viewport: Headline and email field left, a config snippet and inbox screenshot right, three benefits below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
